churches.name: Cornerstone Chapel, an Apostolic Church

score_notes.christology: Oneness Apostolic theology rejects the Trinity — teaches Jesus-Only modalism (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not distinct persons but modes of one God = Jesus). This is a historic heresy (condemned at Nicaea/Constantinople).
score_notes.soteriology: Apostolic churches typically teach baptismal regeneration and speaking in tongues as necessary for salvation — 'Acts 2:38 salvation plan' that adds works to justification by faith alone.
score_notes.gender: Male lead pastor (Robert Eaby Jr.); Oneness Pentecostal tradition historically allows women in various ministry roles; no explicit patriarchal household or male-elder-only framework confirmed.
score_notes.denominational: Apostolic/Oneness tradition stands outside Nicene orthodoxy; no accountability to historic trinitarian Christianity.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel is an Apostolic/Oneness Pentecostal church — and that's a hard stop for theological alignment. Oneness Pentecostalism denies the eternal distinction of the three persons of the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), teaching instead that 'Jesus' is the only name of God and the three are merely different modes. This places it outside the bounds of Nicene orthodoxy — the same line historic Christianity drew in 325 AD. Additionally, most Apostolic churches teach that speaking in tongues and baptism in 'Jesus' name only' are necessary for salvation, adding works to justification. The congregation may be sincere and passionate, but the core theological framework disqualifies it for anyone committed to trinitarian Christianity and faith-alone soteriology. Not recommended.
churches.gender_detail: Male lead pastor; Apostolic tradition varies — women's ministry role unclear in Oneness Pentecostalism

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg UMC sits squarely in the post-split United Methodist Church — the branch that retained 'United Methodist' branding after the traditional/conservative wing departed to form the Global Methodist Church. The 2024 UMC General Conference removed all language restricting LGBTQ+ ordination and same-sex marriage. With a female senior pastor, multiple associate pastors, and UMC denominational accountability to a now-affirming hierarchy, this church does not align with Moop's theological convictions. The congregation may have sincere Christ-loving people in the pews, but the institutional framework is compromised.
churches.gender_detail: Female senior pastor; UMC formally affirms women at all levels and LGBTQ+ clergy/marriage — actively egalitarian

churches.name: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg

score_notes.gender: Calvary Chapel movement holds male pastoral leadership as standard. Mark Ramirez leads as senior pastor; male-only elder/pastor structure is normative in CC churches. Complementarian (halfway house — not fully patriarchal) conviction built into CC DNA.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Joe Gallegos serves as dedicated Men's Ministry leader on staff — an explicit men's discipleship investment.
score_notes.denominational: Calvary Chapel Association is a loose affiliation rather than a formal denomination; provides some accountability but less structured than SBC or PCA.

churches.assessment: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg checks most of the boxes Moop cares about. The Calvary Chapel movement is known above all for verse-by-verse expository Bible teaching — it's baked into the DNA (Chuck Smith legacy). The leadership page shows a clear elder/pastor structure with male pastoral leadership, a dedicated Men's Ministry leader (Joe Gallegos), and a full complement of ministries including youth, children, prayer, and outreach. CC churches typically hold to Scripture inerrancy, salvation by grace through faith alone, and complementarian leadership. The charismatic-adjacent culture (CC is Spirit-friendly but not charismatic in the more extreme sense) may be a moderate fit for Moop's background. The verse-by-verse preaching model is one of the best in evangelical Christianity. Strong candidate.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only pastoral leadership; Calvary Chapel maintains complementarian DNA with male elders and pastors

churches.assessment: Trinity Episcopal has the same fundamental problem as St. George's Episcopal: it belongs to The Episcopal Church (TEC), which has made formal, binding institutional commitments to LGBTQ+ affirmation that place it outside biblical alignment. The rector lists she/her pronouns on the church website, men serve with he/him pronouns listed — pronoun-aware staff culture is a visible marker of TEC's progressive institutional identity. Founded in 1877, Trinity has a rich liturgical history and likely has sincere Christians in the congregation, but the denominational framework and leadership culture are incompatible with Moop's convictions. The 'inclusive community of seekers' branding further flags a therapeutic/inclusive ecclesiology rather than a word-and-sacrament Great Commission model. Not recommended.

score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry confirmed on website.
score_notes.denominational: BGAV is the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship-adjacent body in Virginia — moderate theologically, left the SBC years ago over inerrancy and gender issues.

churches.assessment: Chancellor Baptist's doctrinal statement is genuinely solid — they affirm Scripture as God's Word, salvation through Christ alone, eternal security, baptism by immersion, Great Commission evangelism. The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

The mission statement is Christ-centered and kingdom-focused. The church has a meaningful Facebook/social presence with 2,200+ followers. Reviews describe a welcoming community where Pastor Ernest and leadership genuinely love God and their congregation. The Spirit-emphasis framing ('Empowered by the Spirit,' 'transforming presence and power') suggests a charismatic worship culture. Key unknowns: preaching style (expository vs. topical), stance on gender roles, leadership accountability structure. Worth a visit if you're comfortable with a Spirit-forward evangelical culture; go in with questions about elder structure and biblical authority.

Luke Taylor is a sincere pastor with solid theology on the essentials — Christ is the only way, the Bible is authoritative, gender is binary. But structural concerns are real: no elder accountability, women functioning in pastoral roles, and a spiritual formation emphasis that can trend contemplative rather than expository. If you're a man who needs clear authority structures and complementarian conviction, visit with your eyes open. If you're a new believer or seeking family, you'll find genuine love here. Just ask the hard questions early.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Baptist Church is one of the older Baptist congregations in the city, located on historic Princess Anne Street. The mission language is straightforwardly Christ-centered — 'on mission together, striving to continue the work of Christ' with commitments to 'the praise of God and the proclamation of the word of God' and 'the preservation, instruction, and spreading of the Gospel.' That's a healthy public-facing posture. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream, separate from SBC, and the denominational structure allows women in pastoral roles and leans progressive on several fronts. Pastor David Haun's theological convictions are unknown. Before visiting, Moop should confirm the church's stance on Scripture inerrancy, women in ministry, and elder accountability. The Princess Anne address is prime downtown Fredericksburg — a historic congregation worth investigating.

churches.name: Fredericksburg Church of Christ
churches.pastor: Unknown (Churches of Christ tradition does not use 'pastor' title formally — led by elders)
churches.services: Sunday Bible Study 9:00 AM, Sunday Worship 10:00 AM, Wednesday Bible Study 7:00 PM

score_notes.christology: Churches of Christ affirm Christ as the only Savior; Trinitarian orthodoxy affirmed.
score_notes.scripture: Churches of Christ hold a high view of Scripture as the sole rule of faith and practice — this is central to Restoration Movement identity. Their public statement: 'We plead for religious unity among all believers based on the Bible.'
score_notes.gender: Traditional Churches of Christ consistently hold male-only eldership with women not serving in teaching authority over men. This congregation follows the traditional CoC pattern. Green on gender specifically — soteriology is the concern, not gender roles.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led structure is standard in Churches of Christ — a plurality of male elders is the norm, which is more accountable and biblical than single-pastor models.
score_notes.soteriology: Red flag: Churches of Christ historically teach baptismal regeneration — that water baptism (immersion) is necessary for salvation, not just a response to salvation. The classic formula is 'believe + repent + be baptized = receive Holy Spirit + forgiveness.' This adds a work to justification, which is incompatible with faith-alone soteriology.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/progressive cultural language found; mission statement is straightforwardly Bible-centered.
score_notes.preaching: Churches of Christ are known for verse-by-verse Bible teaching; expository DNA is strong.
score_notes.denominational: Self-described as non-denominational but part of the Churches of Christ tradition — a distinct stream with its own theological DNA (restoration, baptism, a cappella worship in most congregations).

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Church of Christ has a lot going for it: high Scripture authority, Trinitarian orthodoxy, complementarian leadership with male elder plurality, expository DNA, and no cultural drift indicators. The congregation explicitly states they are 'not a denomination, but simply Christians that belong to the body of believers of which Christ is the head' — that's a healthy posture. The hard stop for a faith-alone evangelical like Moop: Churches of Christ traditionally teach that baptism is necessary for salvation, not merely a sign of it. This is the theological fault line that separates the Restoration Movement from mainstream evangelicalism — and it's a real one. Not a cult, not heresy in the broad sense, but incompatible with sola fide. Worth a conversation with leadership to clarify their exact position on baptism and salvation before getting deeper. Some congregations in this tradition have moved toward a more grace-emphasis soteriology; some have not.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only eldership and leadership (Churches of Christ tradition); no women in teaching authority over men

score_notes.christology: Catholic Church affirms Christ as the only Savior; Trinitarian orthodoxy at the highest level — this is Nicene Christianity.
score_notes.scripture: Catholic theology holds Scripture and Sacred Tradition as co-equal sources of revelation — not sola scriptura. The Magisterium (teaching authority of the Church) interprets Scripture authoritatively. This is the classic Protestant/Catholic divide.
score_notes.gender: Roman Catholic Church maintains male-only ordained priesthood — women cannot be priests. However, Catholic teaching does not frame this in terms of biblical patriarchy or husbandly headship in the household; sacramental/apostolic succession theology differs from evangelical complementarian framework. Yellow by framework.
score_notes.leadership: Full hierarchical accountability: parish → diocese → Rome. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane (area dean), signaling senior status. Excellent accountability structure.
score_notes.soteriology: Catholic soteriology includes faith but also sacraments, merit, purgatory, and indulgences — not sola fide. Salvation involves cooperation with grace through the sacramental life of the Church. This is the core Reformation divide.
score_notes.cultural: Diocese of Arlington is one of the most theologically conservative dioceses in the U.S. — less progressive than many other dioceses. No explicit DEI language found on parish website.
score_notes.preaching: Catholic homilies are typically brief (8-12 min), tied to the Sunday Lectionary cycle rather than expository book-by-book preaching.
score_notes.mission: Great Commission is affirmed in Catholic theology; St. Mary is described as 'an active, thriving parish with numerous clubs, organizations, and activities.'
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Knights of Columbus or other men's organizations are standard in active Catholic parishes like St. Mary's.
score_notes.denominational: Excellent accountability: Diocese of Arlington is conservative and supervised; full apostolic succession and diocesan governance.

churches.assessment: Saint Mary's is a large, active Catholic parish in Fredericksburg under the conservative Diocese of Arlington. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane — essentially the area dean — indicating a significant, well-resourced congregation. Trinitarian orthodoxy is rock-solid; male-only priesthood is firmly complementarian; accountability structure is hierarchical and thorough. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the theological divergence is real: Catholic soteriology adds sacraments, merit, and ecclesial mediation to faith; Scripture sits alongside Tradition rather than above it. These are not minor differences — they were the substance of the Reformation. That said, for a man interested in robust liturgy, deep historical tradition, strong pro-life stance, and conservative moral theology, the Diocese of Arlington Catholic experience is among the best available. Not the right fit for a faith-alone evangelical, but should be evaluated on its own terms.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only priesthood (Catholic doctrine) but no explicit biblical patriarchal household framework

churches.review_findings: fbcbeaufort.org is confirmed to be First Baptist Church Beaufort NORTH CAROLINA (403 Ann Street, Beaufort NC 28516, Reverend Bill Brummett). In Beaufort SC, there is no church currently operating as 'First Baptist Church Beaufort.' The historic SBC-affiliated Baptist church in Beaufort SC is 'The Baptist Church of Beaufort' (bcob.org, 601 Charles Street, Beaufort SC) — founded 1804, oldest surviving congregation in town, SC Baptist Convention affiliated. Other Beaufort SC Baptist churches include First African Baptist Church (fabbeaufort.org, Pastor Alexander McBride) and Victory Baptist Church (independent fundamental, 378 Parris Island Gateway).
churches.review_question: The record identity 'First Baptist Beaufort SC' may not correspond to any real church. Delete the record, or rename/redirect to 'The Baptist Church of Beaufort' (bcob.org) which is the historic SBC church at that location? This requires judgment on whether to change church identity.

churches.name: Veritas Bible Church

score_notes.christology: Scripture-centered; affirms Jesus as the Word of eternal life (John 6:68-69).
score_notes.scripture: Strong emphasis on studying Scripture together; Bible is central to identity. References John 8:31-32, Psalm 19:7-9.
score_notes.gender: PATRIARCHAL — per member testimony (Vlad Yakubets): "Men are the rulers of God's world in every sphere of life." This is not halfway-house complementarianism — this is full patriarchal household vision. Green.
score_notes.leadership: Pastoral team with preaching pastor and lead pastor. Verify elder structure.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed/evangelical orientation evident from liturgical approach.
score_notes.cultural: Bible church tradition — typically resistant to cultural drift.
score_notes.denominational: Independent Bible church — no external denominational accountability. The independence is a structural risk, but the patriarchal culture and strong biblical teaching provide internal guardrails. Yellow.
score_notes.preaching: Expository approach evident from emphasis on 'examining biblical texts communally.' Active sermon playlists and YouTube channel.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Annual men's retreat. Men's small groups where men do things independently. No official "men's discipleship program" — but as Vlad notes, when a church is already structured patriarchally, a formal program is redundant. The church's entire culture IS men's discipleship. Green.
score_notes.mission: Active community engagement; Bible reading plans and resources offered.

churches.assessment: Veritas Bible Church in Federal Way, WA is one of the strongest finds in the Pacific Northwest. Member Vlad Yakubets confirms the church holds a PATRIARCHAL (not merely complementarian) view — "men are the rulers of God's world in every sphere of life." This is the full biblical manhood vision. Annual men's retreat and men's small groups provide masculine discipleship without bureaucratic programming. Expository preaching, Scripture-centered identity ("Veritas" = truth), Reformed/evangelical theology. The only yellow is independence (no denominational accountability) — but when the culture is this sound, that's a minor concern. Personally recommended by Vlad Yakubets. One of the few GREEN churches in the entire Pacific Northwest.
churches.gender_detail: Patriarchal — men as rulers in every sphere of life per member testimony. Not merely complementarian. Male pastoral leadership confirmed.

churches.assessment: Eastside Baptist Church in Twin Falls, Idaho is a 1689 Confessional Reformed Baptist church with a plurality of elders, age-integrated worship, and a robust confessional foundation. Founded in 1972, this church holds to the full 1689 London Baptist Confession including the appendix on baptism. The elder-led structure (Thompson, Martinez) with deacons reflects biblical governance. Their adoption of resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription demonstrates a church willing to take stands on cultural issues from Scripture — not hiding behind neutrality. Men's Book Study and age-integrated model mean men are formed as household leaders, not shuffled into a separate program. Four services per week (Sunday AM, Sunday PM, Sunday School, Wednesday evening) indicates a serious, committed congregation. This is an all-GREEN church — rare and worthy of attention for any Reformed Baptist in the Pacific Northwest.

churches.assessment: First Baptist Hammond is one of the most controversial churches in American Christianity. Founded 1887, it became a megachurch under Jack Hyles. The church has been plagued by scandals: Jack Schaap (Hyles' successor and son-in-law) was convicted of transporting a minor across state lines for sexual activity (2012). Multiple staff/associated pastors have faced similar charges. The institutional culture has been widely criticized for prioritizing numbers, easy-believism, and personality-driven leadership over genuine accountability. Current pastor John Wilkerson has attempted to restore credibility, but the institutional DNA remains a major concern. NOT recommended without extensive personal investigation.

churches.name: Elevation Church
churches.services: Saturday 5:00 PM; Sunday 9:30 AM, 11:30 AM (varies by campus; 20 locations)
churches.assessment: Elevation Church is a megachurch (17,000+ weekly attendance, 20 campuses) led by Steven Furtick. SBC-affiliated but operates independently with minimal denominational accountability. Furtick is controversial: prosperity-adjacent theology, celebrity pastor model, modalist-leaning statements on the Trinity (2014 controversy), heavy emphasis on vision-casting over expository preaching. Topical/motivational preaching style. No men's discipleship emphasis found. Address in data (1 Elevation Way, Matthews) is correct for HQ. Massive online presence. Theologically, this is a YELLOW-to-RED church depending on the rubric — entertainment-driven worship, weak on doctrinal precision, personality cult around Furtick.

churches.name: NewSpring Church
churches.pastor: Team leadership model (Lead Pastors: Brad Cooper, Michael Mullikin, Tyler Tatum, David Hall, Lee McDerment, Riley Cummings)
churches.assessment: NewSpring Church — SBC megachurch, 13 campuses across SC. Founder Perry Noble was FIRED in July 2016 for alcohol abuse and family neglect. Church transitioned to team leadership model. Anderson campus pastor is Allen Cothran. NOTE: Teaching pastor list includes Meredith Knox — a FEMALE teaching pastor who shares the stage on Sundays. This is a concern for complementarian evaluation. The church's history of pastoral moral failure (Noble) and current team-leadership-with-female-teaching-pastor model raises significant questions.

churches.name: Life.Church
churches.services: Saturday 4:00 PM, 5:30 PM; Sunday 8:30, 10:00, 11:30 AM, 1:00 PM (Edmond campus)
churches.assessment: Life.Church is one of the largest churches in America, led by Craig Groeschel since 1996. Multi-site model with video-venue preaching (Groeschel preaches via screen at most campuses). Created the YouVersion Bible App. Massive digital/online presence. Theologically broad evangelical — topical preaching, seeker-sensitive model. No strong men's discipleship emphasis found. Groeschel lives in Edmond with wife Amy and six children. Church is personality-driven but Groeschel has maintained a clean public record. Denomination listed as Evangelical Covenant but operates essentially as non-denominational megachurch.

churches.name: Asbury Church Tulsa
churches.assessment: Asbury Church Tulsa — FORMERLY United Methodist, DISAFFILIATED in 2022 over theological differences. Nearly 7,000 members. Now operates as independent 'Asbury Church.' Disaffiliation was driven by UMC's drift from historic Christian mission, particularly on sexuality issues. Considering joining Global Methodist Church (conservative Methodist denomination). Pastor Tom Harrison led the disaffiliation; Andrew Forrest is current Senior Pastor. Founded 1962. The disaffiliation over orthodoxy is a POSITIVE indicator — they left because the UMC was too progressive. Statement of faith available on their website.

Rebranded from Highland Park Baptist in January 2013 after sale of downtown Chattanooga campus; relocated to Camp Joy property in Harrison, TN under Dr. Jeremy Roberts.

churches.assessment: Christ Church Nashville — 'three streams' congregation (liturgical, evangelical, charismatic). Known for music and inspirational worship. 'Three streams' and AMiA ordination makes this theologically unique — not standard evangelical. L.H. Hardwick was previous long-time pastor. Interdenominational identity. Needs further doctrinal evaluation.

churches.name: Fellowship Memphis
churches.address: 600 S Shady Grove Rd, Memphis, TN 38120
churches.pastor: John Bryson (co-founder; Bryan Loritts was co-founder but left in 2015)
churches.assessment: Fellowship Memphis — Acts 29 multi-ethnic church. MAJOR CONCERN: Co-founder Bryan Loritts was involved in a scandal where worship pastor Rick Trotter (Loritts' brother-in-law) secretly recorded women and possibly children in a church bathroom in 2010. Allegations that leadership (including co-founder John Bryson) discouraged victims from going to police. Loritts left in 2015 for NYC. Guidepost investigation found 'errors of judgment' but 'no concrete evidence of cover-up.' Located at 1100 Cherry Rd (not 600 S Shady Grove). Currently gospel-centered, disciple-making, multi-ethnic mission. The scandal history is a significant concern for due diligence.

score_notes.scripture: Begg is a committed inerrantist. Scripture is the final authority in all matters of faith and practice. Every sermon is text-driven.

score_notes.preaching: World-class expository preaching. Begg is widely regarded as one of the finest verse-by-verse preachers alive. Truth For Life broadcasts reach millions.

score_notes.mens_discipleship: Men's ministry and discipleship groups available.

churches.assessment: Parkside Church under Alistair Begg is one of the premier expository Bible-teaching churches in America. Begg has preached verse-by-verse through Scripture for over 40 years with unwavering commitment to inerrancy, male headship, and the exclusivity of Christ. Truth For Life radio ministry extends his influence globally. The church is elder-led, missions-minded, and doctrinally rock-solid. A top-tier GREEN church. Note: Begg drew controversy in late 2023 for advising a grandmother to attend a grandchild's transgender wedding — he later clarified his pastoral intent but the incident raised some concerns among discernment circles.

churches.assessment: The Moody Church is one of the most historically significant evangelical churches in America, rooted in the legacy of D.L. Moody. Dr. Erwin Lutzer served as the 16th pastor for 36 years (1980-2016), establishing it as a bastion of conservative evangelical theology. Dr. Philip Miller became the 17th Senior Pastor in 2020. The church is at the intersection of North Ave, Clark St, and LaSalle St in Chicago. Deep commitment to biblical authority, missions, and expository preaching. A historic evangelical landmark.
churches.denomination_detail: Non-denominational / Independent — historic church founded in D.L. Moody tradition. Building dedicated 1925.

churches.assessment: New Life Church has a troubled history. Founded by Ted Haggard (removed 2006 for sexual misconduct), then led by Brady Boyd (2007-2025) who resigned after the church elders determined he was dishonest about what he knew regarding Robert Morris's sexual abuse of a child. Boyd had served at Gateway Church under Morris. Two consecutive pastoral scandals involving sexual misconduct/cover-ups is a severe red flag for institutional culture and accountability. Daniel Grothe (ORU-trained) now serves as interim pastor. The Oral Roberts University connection also signals charismatic/Pentecostal theological orientation. Not recommended given the pattern of leadership failures.

churches.assessment: Jesse Duplantis Ministries is a prosperity gospel operation. Duplantis famously asked donors to fund a $54 million private jet, claiming God told him he needed it. He teaches that financial giving to his ministry unlocks divine blessing — classic prosperity gospel exploitation. His theology is Word of Faith heresy dressed up in folksy humor. No accountability, extreme personal wealth from ministry funds, and a false gospel. Disqualified.

churches.name: Andrew Wommack Ministries / Charis Bible College
churches.type: Charismatic / Word of Faith / Bible School

score_notes.christology: Basic Christology but Word of Faith framework distorts.
score_notes.scripture: Positive confession theology; Scripture filtered through Word of Faith lens.
score_notes.preaching: Word of Faith teaching; not expository.
score_notes.mission: Bible college graduates carry Word of Faith theology worldwide.

churches.assessment: Andrew Wommack Ministries operates Charis Bible College and teaches a Word of Faith / charismatic theology. Wommack's teaching emphasizes healing as always God's will, positive confession theology, and a framework that can blame sick believers for lacking faith. While less flamboyant than some prosperity teachers, the theological framework still distorts Scripture. His Bible college produces graduates steeped in this framework. Red rating for Word of Faith theology and accountability concerns.

churches.name: Gateway Church
churches.pastor: Interim leadership (Robert Morris resigned 2024 after abuse allegations)

score_notes.scripture: Bible taught but prosperity-adjacent hermeneutic (tithing theology).
score_notes.leadership: Catastrophic accountability failure — founder resigned after abuse allegations.
score_notes.mission: Large missions program but institutional crisis.

churches.assessment: Gateway Church was one of the largest mega-churches in America under Robert Morris, who resigned in 2024 after credible allegations of childhood sexual abuse surfaced. The church has strong charismatic elements, including tithing theology that borders on prosperity gospel (Morris' 'The Blessed Life' teaching). Leadership accountability clearly failed catastrophically. The church is in transition but the theological and governance framework that enabled the scandal remains a concern. Red rating for scandal, charismatic excess, and accountability failure.

churches.name: Granger Community Church
churches.assessment: Granger Community Church near South Bend, IN was one of the early megachurches in the Midwest. Known for creative arts-driven services. Seeker-sensitive model. Verify current theological direction and leadership.

churches.name: The Chapel
churches.assessment: The Chapel in Akron carries the legacy of Knute Larson, one of the great Bible expositors. Large multi-site church in northeast Ohio. Generally conservative, Bible-teaching tradition. Strong expository heritage.

churches.name: Central Christian Church
churches.assessment: Central Christian Church is the largest church in the Las Vegas metro. Led by Jud Wilhite. Restoration Movement heritage. Seeker-sensitive, creative services. Generally evangelical. Verify doctrinal specifics.

churches.name: Sun Valley Community Church

churches.name: Canyon Ridge Christian Church

churches.assessment: First Presbyterian Church of Columbia, South Carolina (ARP) is one of the most historically significant orthodox Reformed congregations in the United States. The 1854 church building is on the National Register of Historic Places (added January 1971). The pulpit lineage includes James Henley Thornwell, Benjamin Morgan Palmer, John Girardeau, and more recently Sinclair Ferguson and Derek Thomas — a roll call of Reformed theological heavyweights. The congregation principled-seceded from the mainline Presbyterian Church in the United States in 1983 and joined the ARP to preserve its confessional identity. Dr. Neil C. Stewart currently serves as Senior Minister and Head of Staff. Three Sunday services (8:30 AM, 11:15 AM, and 6:00 PM). ARP confessional framework with male-only ordination aligns with MOOP's biblical-design rubric. One of the strongest possible green-rated Reformed Presbyterian options in the Southeast, though note that the church's website currently displays 'Presbyterian Church (USA)' in some metadata — this appears to be outdated website text; per the ARP official directory and Wikipedia, the church has been ARP since 1983.

This is textbook confessional Continental Reformed practice — no women in office, no cultural drift, serious catechetical formation for children and adults.
